kill_fact: No kill available: every load-bearing bear number reconciles to the primary source. The Q2 2026 results release (29 July 2026) confirms the segment table the bear case rests on to the dollar -- Combat Systems revenue $2,290M vs $2,283M (+0.3%) with operating earnings FALLING to $318M from $324M and margin 13.9% vs 14.2%; Technologies $3,619M vs $3,476M (+4.1%) with margin 9.4% vs 9.6%; Marine Systems margin 7.3% -- and confirms H1 2026 free cash flow of $3.598B on capital expenditure of only $437M (1.6% of H1 revenue against a 3.5-4.0% full-year guide), which is the arithmetic behind the ~$1.2B second-half cash step-down. The 10-Q balance sheet dated 5 July 2026 confirms the sum-of-the-parts net debt of $5.146B (total debt $9.479B including $1.963B of finance leases, less $4.333B cash) and 273.8M diluted shares, and confirms there is no structural floor -- the company is net-debt, not net-cash. The FIRED catalyst is real and primary-sourced: the company's own 29 July 2026 release states $42.1B for nine Virginia-class and $29.5B for five Columbia-class boats within a $76.6B Navy award. The one genuine defect is a peer anchor: the bear prices Leidos at 8.2x EV/EBITDA and uses that number both rhetorically ('more than double Leidos') and as the explicit justification for the 9x multiple on the Technologies leg of the adverse case. Leidos was not at 8.2x on the record's own as-of date -- it closed at $130.60 on 4 August 2026, implying roughly 9.7x EV/EBITDA, and stands at 10.27x on 11 August 2026. 8.2x corresponds to a Leidos price near $103, last seen before the late-July re-rating. Correcting the anchor lifts the adverse-case Technologies leg and the bear price with it.
corrections: (1) LEIDOS ANCHOR STALE. sop_bear values Technologies at 9x operating earnings, justified as 'the risk the market already prices into Leidos at 8.2 times EBITDA'. Leidos EV/EBITDA was ~9.7x on 4 August 2026 (close $130.60; EV ~$22.3B on ~$2.29B TTM EBITDA) and is 10.27x on 11 August 2026 (EV $23.52B). Re-anchoring proportionally gives 9 x (9.7/8.2) = 10.6x, so Technologies = $1.22B x 10.6 = $12.9B against the record's $10.9B. Adverse-case enterprise value becomes $66.9B ($23.7 + $19.0 + $15.1 + $12.9 - $3.8), less the record's own $5.146B net debt and $0.5B committed pension contribution = $61.3B over 273.8M diluted shares = $224. The companion rhetorical claim that GD trades at 'more than double Leidos' also fails: 16.9x against 10.3x is 1.6x, not 2x. (2) QUARTER-END DATE WRONG. catalyst_status_note states the reported $136.5B backlog 'closed on 28 June' and that the award 'post-dates the 28 June quarter close'. The filed quarter ended 5 JULY 2026. The conclusion is unaffected -- the 29 July award post-dates either date and is genuinely excluded from the $136.5B -- but the date itself is wrong. (3) PRICE DRIFT AGAINST THE RECORD. Live price is $393.60 on 11 August 2026 against the record's $386.99 as of 4 August (+1.7%). The risk_reward conclusion strengthens rather than weakens: the price now sits 21% above the $325 base case, the corrected adverse case is 43% below, and the bull case only 9% above -- roughly one dollar of upside for every 4.7 of identified downside. (4) NOT CORRECTED, VERIFIED. The gm_trajectory rebuttal of the 'compressing' proxy holds exactly against filed statements: TTM gross margin 15.38% ($8.435B on $54.861B) against 15.40% a year earlier, with Q1 2026 at 15.90% vs 15.49% and Q2 2026 at 15.49% vs 14.94%. Flat, not eroding. Bear pillars one, three and five (two stalled segments at 41.9% of revenue, the guided second-half cash reversal, the peer-premium multiple) all survive. Bear pillar two -- that the newly definitized Block VI and Build II contracts leave inflation risk with the builder -- remains UNVERIFIED in either direction, and the record is candid that nobody has asked; it is a stated risk, not an established fact, and should not be scored as one. (5) ONE POST-AS-OF DATAPOINT CUTS AGAINST THE BEAR: GDIT was awarded a $1.3B Army National Guard ENOCS contract on 7 August 2026, an order win in the segment the bear calls structurally stalled -- an order, not revenue, so it does not move the numbers.
